links.outcome: Time from CXR to lung cancer diagnosis; cost-effectiveness of AI worklist prioritisation
links.effect: AI prioritisation did not reduce time to diagnosis and was not cost-effective vs AI without prioritisation; budget impact £2 million per year in England.
links.quote: The LungIMPACT randomised study found that the use of an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to flag and prioritise chest X-rays (CXR) referred from primary care in the human reporter’s worklist, did not reduce time from CXR to lung cancer (LC) diagnosis.

links.outcome: Cost-effectiveness and budget impact of AI vs no AI
links.effect: No AI was always more cost-effective; budget impact £16–35 million per year for AI comparisons vs No AI.
links.quote: AI with prioritisation was not cost-effective vs. AI without prioritisation and secondary analysis showed that no AI was always more cost-effective.
